title: DEC-106: Defer dormant seller liveness from launch (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-106: Defer dormant seller liveness from launch (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: The launch IA declared `dormant` but could not reach it because no seller-session-recency producer or product sanction existed; hiding could falsely remove a touring musician's income surface.
- **Options considered**: Defer `dormant`; launch it as browse/search demotion only; launch it by hiding the shopfront.
- **Decision**: Defer `dormant`. Launch listing liveness contains only `responsive` and `stale`; qualifying listings remain `stale`, browse/search-demoted, and directly accessible. Preserve the 60-day plus at least three unanswered requests predicate only as deferred policy.
- **Downstream**: Resolve 05.01.01 Q-06; remove `dormant`, its sanction, and seller-session-recency producer from launch IA contracts; require `/evolve-feature` before future activation.
- **Reversibility**: High

title: DEC-107: Extend MandateGrant for live-performance reporting (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-107: Extend MandateGrant for live-performance reporting (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: Shard 19 permits territory-scoped operator filing but canonical `MandateGrant` has no live-performance reporting activity or territory/body scope.
- **Options considered**: Extend canonical `MandateGrant`; add a Shard 19 subordinate reporting grant; remove operator filing and permit performer filing only.
- **Decision**: Extend canonical `MandateGrant` with a closed `report_live_performance` activity plus act/principal, collecting-body, and territory scope. Reuse existing effective interval, authority ceiling, attribution, expiry, and transitive-revocation semantics. Shard 19 references this canonical grant and still requires the reporter's own `pro_membership_id`; another party's accreditation never transfers.
- **Downstream**: Propagate activity and scope fields through Shard 01 registry, authority resolution, revocation, deep dive, and reciprocal Shard 19 contract; update Shard 19 access rules, reporting algorithm, failure behavior, and deep dive.
- **Reversibility**: Medium

title: DEC-108: Use audited manual disposition for offline name collisions (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-108: Use audited manual disposition for offline name collisions (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: Offline door name lookup can return multiple attendees, but no low-risk discriminator is universal across paid tickets, transfers, comps, free RSVPs, eye-check admission, and external tickets. Replicating postcode or arbitrary PII would violate the minimal encrypted replica posture.
- **Options considered**: No secondary PII and closed audited manual disposition; normalized booking/order-reference suffix; normalized postcode fragment.
- **Decision**: Use no secondary PII offline. On multiple normalized-name matches, an authorized operator chooses exactly one closed outcome: `deferred_for_online_reconciliation`, `operator_admitted_under_exception`, or `refused_unresolved_collision`. Append-only audit records event, replica epoch, device, gate, operator, candidate-count band, outcome, reason code, timestamp, and reconciliation state; they never record postcode, date of birth, address, identification document, or arbitrary operator-entered PII.
- **Downstream**: Update Shard 36 DoorReplica lookup, operator authorization, manual-disposition entity and closed vocabularies, audit/reconciliation rules, retention/wipe rules, typed refusals, existence-leakage controls, offline collision algorithm, and deep-dive failure paths.
- **Reversibility**: Medium

title: DEC-110: Use proportional expected-no-show shortfall (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-110: Use proportional expected-no-show shortfall (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: Pre-close alert promised an independent-source comparison but defined no operands, formula, unit, threshold, or boundary.
- **Options considered**: Proportional independent-source shortfall; absolute headcount shortfall; combined absolute and proportional gate; defer executable alert.
- **Decision**: Compute `shortfall_people = max(0, external_expected_attendance - internal_admissions)` and `shortfall_bps = floor(shortfall_people * 10000 / external_expected_attendance)`. Alert when `shortfall_bps >= expected_no_show.shortfall_alert_bps`. External operand is fresh operator-confirmed `expected_attendance`; internal operand is pinned `admissions_total` from same show/count version, unless `CountMapping` explicitly declares paid-only basis. Threshold is required in versioned per-show policy with no hidden default. Zero expected attendance returns `EXPECTED_ATTENDANCE_ZERO`; stale source returns `SOURCE_STALE`; paid/total mismatch returns `BASIS_MISMATCH`; absent policy returns `POLICY_UNCONFIGURED`. Alert carries headcount and basis-point shortfall, source/version references, freshness, policy version, and evaluation timestamp; it never chooses settlement figure or resolves source disagreement.
- **Downstream**: Update Shard 36 expected-attendance semantics, count basis mapping, policy reference, alert event, formula, integer rounding, inclusive boundary, typed outcomes, and deep dive; confirm Shard 31 settlement semantics remain unchanged.
- **Reversibility**: High

title: DEC-111: Apportion bundles by pinned standalone prices (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-111: Apportion bundles by pinned standalone prices (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: Single-vendor bundle consideration needed deterministic per-item allocation before existing cent-remainder handling, because refunds and contributor amounts consume persisted allocations.
- **Options considered**: Proportional to pinned standalone prices; vendor-declared versioned weights; equal allocation across eligible items.
- **Decision**: Resolve ownership first and remove already-owned items. Pin every eligible item's authoritative standalone price and version. Allocate ownership-adjusted settled consideration proportional to those pinned prices, then apply Shard 18's existing largest-remainder cent rule. Prices must be nonnegative integer minor units in transaction currency; allocated values must be nonnegative and sum exactly to settled consideration. Persist allocation-policy ID/version with each `PromotionAllocation`. Refuse typed when price is missing, currencies differ, eligible total is zero, ownership is unresolved, or pinned price/policy is stale. Refunds, entitlement accounting, contributor accrual, and payout consume persisted allocation and never recalculate from current prices.
- **Downstream**: Update Shard 28 bundle policy, ownership-before-pricing order, `SavePromotion`, cart-line allocation snapshot, `PromotionAllocation`, refunds, contributor accrual, payout consumption, typed outcomes, event contract, and blocked-dependency text. Do not redefine Shard 18 residue policy.
- **Reversibility**: Medium

title: DEC-112: Pin flag dependencies and experiment consent policy versions (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-112: Pin flag dependencies and experiment consent policy versions (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: `FeatureFlagVersion.dependencies` and `ExperimentVersion.consent_ref` had no target identity, cardinality, or retention contract.
- **Options considered**: Immutable flag-version references plus Shard 05 `ExperimentConsentPolicyVersion`; mutable flag-key references resolved at activation; external canonical privacy-contract entity; opaque text/UUID references.
- **Decision**: Each flag dependency targets exactly one immutable `FeatureFlagVersion` by `(key, version)`; one target may have zero-to-many referrers. Publication rejects missing, duplicate, self, cyclic, or already-retired targets. New dependency versions never alter existing referrers; graph changes require new referring versions. Referenced versions cannot be destructively deleted; expiry/retirement preserves history and replay. `ExperimentVersion.consent_ref` is zero-or-one to exactly one immutable Shard 05 `ExperimentConsentPolicyVersion`. Policy records analytics purpose, subject/cohort scope, admissible dimensions, effective interval, legal/privacy provenance, withdrawal behavior, and version. It documents permission provenance but grants no product access, identity, legal status, or business eligibility. Withdrawal/expiry stops new assignment immediately; historical exposure and referenced policy remain retained and non-destructible.
- **Downstream**: Update Shard 05 typed dependency model, inverse cardinality, cycle/publication validation, retirement/deletion, consent-policy entity, experiment target/cardinality, withdrawal/retention, typed publish failures, deep-dive graph replay, activation/fallback, and consent validation.
- **Reversibility**: Medium

title: DEC-109: Use versioned bounded same-device scan dedupe (2026-08-09)
text:
### DEC-109: Use versioned bounded same-device scan dedupe (2026-08-09)
- **Problem**: Same-device duplicate handling referenced an undefined dedupe window, allowing incompatible count and audit behavior.
- **Options considered**: Versioned 30-second default with bounded per-show override; global versioned 30-second window; epoch-scoped idempotency without a time window; global versioned 10-second window.
- **Decision**: Add `door.same_device_repeat_dedupe_seconds` as integer seconds with default `30`, permitted range `1..300`, and inclusive boundary (`elapsed <= configured_seconds`). Identity tuple is `(show_id, device_id, ticket_id, ticket_epoch)`. Use monotonic device elapsed time and retain capture timestamps for audit. Pin setting/version when provisioning event replica; changes apply forward only to newly provisioned or updated replicas. Inside window, re-display exact previous verdict, append no second canonical admission, and mutate no admission, occupancy, fraud, or settlement count. Outside window, append a new attempt; an already-consumed ticket epoch never counts as another admission, and ordinary used-ticket/re-entry policy determines verdict. Offline mode uses replica-pinned value and never a device-local constant.
- **Downstream**: Update Shard 36 setting registry, replica/configuration contract, scan-attempt and count projections, same-device algorithm, boundary behavior, offline behavior, and deep dive; test below, at, and above boundary plus stale settings and epoch changes.
- **Reversibility**: High
